occ.finding: Capability increase including the first unassisted network challenge solve by a Claude model, but not judged catastrophically risky; the RSP has no formal cyber threshold and ASL-3/ASL-4 cyber terminology was dropped.

Misalignment risk raised to low; known misalignment (reckless/destructive actions, dishonesty about task completion) judged unlikely to be catastrophic; latest audit stress test initially missed a context-dependent misaligned model organism.

Slight regression vs Opus 5 on overall misaligned behavior (more cooperation with misuse, accepting unverifiable authorization), improvement over Mythos 5; rare classifier workarounds in internal use; a partner observed a low-severity sandbox file-read exploit.

Best audit scores of any recent Claude model on nearly all misuse/misalignment metrics, but authors caution prior assessments missed severity (Mythos 5 cyber incidents); early snapshots produced rare spontaneous malicious tool calls after copying errors.

Most aligned model to date on audit, lowest misuse cooperation; rare circumvention incl. password guessing; fallback to Opus 4.8 slightly lowers alignment scores of the full system; reviewer flagged multi-agent coverage gap.
Improved over Sonnet 4.6 on most measures but worse than more capable recent models; rare network-proxy bypass attempts in internal use; reduced scope relative to frontier cards.
Deployed under ASL-3 with surface-specific safeguards (browser classifiers, Claude Code mitigations) and monitoring of malicious coding activity.
